original.target_description: Published Study 2, Amazon Mechanical Turk participants, mixed-model GLM comparing elderly Black targets with other targets on novel out-group categorization. The supplied PDF-page-7 locator (printed page 14) contains multiple applicable tests and does not identify which test is assigned.

replication.target_description: Published replication of Makhanova et al. (2015), Study 2: primary mixed-model GLM three-way interaction of experimental pathogen-threat condition, individual differences in germ aversion, and the planned target contrast (elderly Black targets versus the average of the other three target groups), predicting minimal-outgroup categorization in the retained White participant sample.

n.sample_role: Participants retained for the preregistered primary analyses, after exclusions; White online Prime Panels sample.
n.exclusions: 903 recruited; excluded incorrect personality-type recall (n = 198), incorrect manipulation-article topic recall (n = 79), and not self-reporting race as White (n = 137). The sensitivity analysis excluding 41 participants for article-reading time was ancillary, not the primary target analysis.
n.location: Published p. 175 (PDF p. 5), Method—Participants; p. 176 footnote 1 for reading-time sensitivity analysis.

notes:
Both papers independently sought. No full paper text acquired; abstract/publisher preview and secondary descriptions were not used to infer statistics or the authors’ target-specific replication verdict.
Source follow-up: Fresh replication-only blind extraction from the supplied published article text; title, authors, journal pagination, and DOI match the assigned reference. The article identifies its single replication as a replication of the original Study 2 (p. 174), rather than presenting an independently numbered replication Study 2. Selected the explicitly preregistered direct replication three-way interaction on p. 176, matching the supplied pp. 4–6 locator, rather than the exploratory four-level target analysis on p. 178. Requested printed test statistic is retained; the same test also prints partial eta-squared .012. The authors report partial replication overall, including a replicated interaction but no original synergistic age/race pattern. Original side is an unassigned placeholder, not an acquisition-failure determination.
Source follow-up: Original title and DOI verified in the supplied published-article text: /home/lukas/.t3/worktrees/fred-data/audit-fred-stats-2026-10/audit/fred_stats_2026-10/texts/followup_mac_a0e722e14c344d504e3b2bf7.txt. Source version: published article supplied by licensed EBSCO PsycInfo service. Study 2 Results, printed p. 14 (PDF p. 7), reports a target-type main effect, target type × germ aversion interaction, target type × germ aversion × priming condition interaction, and high-germ-aversion target-type simple effect. All concern the supplied broad description; no unique test identifier is supplied, so no one effect-size/p pair is assigned. Method reports forty-four participants and six additional non-White Americans excluded; Results reports two further participants excluded for forgetting the article topic or personality type. An explicit final analytic n is not printed in this passage. All original statistic fields remain null under the required locator_insufficient failure schema. Replication and reported_success are unassigned original-only placeholders; no replication source examined.
